As far as our long - term growth and strategy is concerned, we are quite confident that we would be able to achieve our projected revenue target of Rs.1500 crores by 2031.
Our quarter-to-quarter revenue, this year has grown by 17%, it is not what I expected.
Growth & demand: As far as our consolidated order book condition is concerned, our current order book stands at Rs.932 crore, of which India has Rs.293 crore and outside India the order book is Rs.639 crore, which is quite a healthy sign because the more orders we have outside India, the improved performance on the PAT as well as EBITDA margins.
As you can see, in case of Waterfront we have Rs.34 crore order book , in March Rs.31 crore order book at Ro dney Hunt Rs.

If you add the orders which we have already executed, the revenue till 30th June and the order book we have today you will observe that it is more than Rs.1,080 crores which means that it should be easy for Jash Engineering Limited us to meet our projected Rs.
Margins & costs: Our EBITDA margin also has improved as well as our EBITDA has improved.
What is quite heartening is that the gross profit margin in Q4 and now is nearly same and generally in the Q4 the gross margins are better.

In FAQs, you had mentioned that this year's PAT margin, earlier we were saying 12 -13%, but now post refunds and probably the order book and the execution of Q1, you are thinking 13 -14% is what we should realistically take from PAT margin perspective.
Capex & expansion: So, in US what is the current tariff structure over there, is it 12% 10% special tariff and 5.6% was the existing so 15.6% is the current tariff there Okay and lastly sir on your capex and expansion front what's the current status in terms of Saudi Arabia new plant which we are looking for.

So , what I am saying is my projections of Rs.1500 crore gives me guidance to how to invest in the manufacturing capacity, and as always I have been telling that the manufacturing capacity is flexible.
If I am able to increase from two shift to three shift, the same capacity can add another Rs.100-200 crore in production.
Balance sheet & cash: I mean, are we going to be taking some long-term debt to fund it.

Guidance & outlook: If we are able to do INR875 crore, then our profit guidance would be the range of 12-13%.

Here also I am conservative because the raw material prices are increasing, and so I would not like to be very optimistic on the profit guidance, but 12 -13% is quite conservative, and is easily possible.
So, if we look for margin on standalone basis, FY23 was 14.52%, FY24 was 14.21%, FY25 was 14.39% and FY26 was 13.38%.
Growth & demand: Whenever there is growth lesser than 3-4% in a company like us, overheads always grow 7-10% annually, and when the growth is less than 7-10% we will see that or observe that the profit after tax and before tax comes down, and that is what has happened with us this year.

When we come to order book, as on 1st May, our order book is INR899 crores and this, along with what we have already achieved till 1st May, will ensure that the projected target of INR875 crore can easily be met.
Waterfront order book, as of now, is more than the turnover, nearly GBP3 million is the order book, which was what we had achieved this year as the revenue.
Margins & costs: The domestic business, as I said earlier, has gone up by 18% year on year, and that has been a very predictable performance on the domestic business front, and that also was done with good margin of profit.
So, you have mentioned that we went for revenue versus margin, so we had a 40% revenue growth, but margins that kind of declined a bit.
So, we can say in those portion fairly high PAT margin of 18-20% can be doable if there is no other change of escalation or inflation in steel price.
Capex & expansion: When the R odney Hunt plant in Houston, as well as in Saudi Arabia, is online and working well, I think in five year's time we will have capacity to produce more than INR1500 crore.
Once we are able to bring online Houston plant and the Saudi Arabia plant, we would reach capacity of INR1500 crore plus.
So, the capex incurred during FY26 was more than INR37 crore in plant and machinery and INR30 crore for the acquisition, so total INR67 crore.
Balance sheet & cash: And also, sir, you had mentioned previously that you will be giving standalone and console working capital separately for us to understand the working capital scenario.
So , we just want to understand how fast we are on the working capital, how optimized we are in the domestic versus what is the situation in the overseas.
Risks & challenges: But the risk also is too great, because there is so much of uncertainty today going on in America, that if you are in a project manufacturing environment, not mass production, a project manufacturing environment you never know what would be the new policies .

So, first two years are always challenging, Jash Engineering Limited doesn't matter how good or bad a company is, and once you have overcome those challenges in the first two years, thereafter the phase of growth comes and so we are not much bothered.
So, competition is not an issue, because the steel prices in America today is more than 50% of the prices in India , competition is not an issue .
